about: The one rule about what a row may carry alongside its name, written where both sides of the
wire can be held to it. The server decides what to write onto an option element and the
control decides what to read back off one, so the rule is implemented twice in two languages
and neither implementation can see the other. A name added to one and forgotten in the other
is a row that goes out carrying something that never comes back, which nothing fails on.
Each case is stated in what JSON can say, so both readings can be held to the same words.
Anything only one language can express — an object instance, an undefined — stays a case of
its own beside the reading that has to answer for it.
`reserved` names what an option already stores in its own right, and so what a row's extras
may not claim. It is the part of the rule that grows, so it is stated as a list rather than
buried in a case: a name added here is a name both readings are made to drop.
